items.text: The Wizard of Oz was shown on television for the first time on November 3, 1956, on CBS.
items.question: Where were you the first time you saw The Wizard of Oz on television, and whose set did you watch it on?
items.source_quote: November 3 – MGM's screen classic, The Wizard of Oz, is shown on television for the first time by CBS, as the final installment of their Ford Star Jubilee.

items.text: General Electric/Telechron introduced "The Snooz Alarm", the first snooze alarm clock, on June 8, 1956.
items.question: Who in your house had the first alarm clock with a snooze button, and who was the hardest to get out of bed?
items.source_quote: June 8 – General Electric/Telechron introduces model 7H241 "The Snooz Alarm", first snooze alarm clock.

items.text: Don Larsen of the New York Yankees pitched the only perfect game in World Series history on October 8, 1956, against the Brooklyn Dodgers, and the Yankees won the series.
items.question: Where were you when Don Larsen pitched his perfect game, and who in your family rooted for the Yankees or the Dodgers?
items.source_quote: October 8 – Baseball pitcher Don Larsen of the New York Yankees throws the only perfect game in World Series history in Game 5 of the 1956 World Series against the Brooklyn Dodgers. Yogi Berra catches the game. Dale Mitchell is the final out. The New York Yankees win the series.
